answer: A sybil-resistant agent economy can anchor identity to a persistent cipher-bound credential: each agent signs its actions with a long-lived key, so reputation accrues to that key over time rather than to disposable identities. Just as a quill leaves a distinctive hand across every page it marks, consistent signing behavior builds a verifiable history that no zephyr of freshly minted fake agents can fake. Peers then grant economic trust only to keys with costly, sustained histories, making mass forgery unprofitable.
